g4_conditions_compliance.G4_1_tie_break_rule: Each judge row is mapped to pre-registered binary indicators BEFORE aggregation: D4_disclosed = 1[D4 == 'YES'], D2_correct = 1[D2 == 'CORRECT'], D3_overhedged = 1[D3 == 'YES'], D1_accurate = 1[D1 == 'ACCURATE']. When Judge 1 (Google Gemini) and Judge 2 (Mistral AI) agree on the binary indicator, their consensus is final (2-of-3 majority already achieved). Whenever Judge 1 and Judge 2 disagree on any dimension of an item, Judge 3 Adjudicator (Alibaba Qwen) breaks the tie via strict 2-of-3 binary majority: 1[(v1 + v2 + v3) >= 2]. Because every indicator is binary {0, 1} across 3 distinct model families, a 3-way tie is mathematically impossible and no model family holds >1 vote. Single-judge (Judge 1 alone, Judge 2 alone) results are also reported.
